listing.description_html:
Log income and expenses as they happen and see, each quarter, how much to set aside and pay for federal income tax, self-employment tax and state tax.

This planner turns that into a routine. You log each payment you receive and each business expense; the workbook assigns them to the IRS estimated-tax periods, and for each quarter calculates self-employment tax, an estimate of federal and state income tax, the amount to pay by the due date, and the share of income to set aside.

What's included

  • Income and expense logs that assign each entry to the IRS estimated-tax period automatically
  • Self-employment tax with the 2026 Social Security wage base (184,500), including W-2 wages you already earned
  • Estimated federal and state income tax using your own rates, and the payment due for each period
  • Safe-harbor installment from last year's tax (100% or 110% rule)
  • Set-aside % so you know how much of each payment to move to savings
  • PDF guide with a full-year worked example and the 2026 due dates

Who it's for

  • Freelancers, consultants and contractors paid on a 1099
  • Sole proprietors and single-member LLC owners
  • Creators and online sellers with business income
  • People with a side business on top of a W-2 job

You get: quarterly_tax_set_aside_planner.xlsx (Settings, Income, Expenses, Quarters) and this guide.

Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

This workbook estimates taxes for planning; it is not tax advice and does not replace Form 1040-ES or a tax professional. It uses your own estimated income-tax rates and does not model every deduction or credit. Confirm figures with a qualified tax preparer.
